Projected from docs/v15/the60_v15_assembly.step by hidden-line projection, with dimension text written from docs/v15/the60_v15/src/params.py. No hand drafting. The knob is drawn on its turned profile: the knurl is on the part but is not drawn.
MODELLED, NOT MADE — no v15 part has been produced. Dimensions are model values, not inspection results. Bodies tagged ENVELOPE or ASSUMED in the model are drawn as envelopes, not as the real part.
SECTION B-B scale 1.05 : 1
Right half, on the 310 deg - 130 deg axis, through the encoder at 310 deg. The whole vertical stack, pad to lens.
CL

z 31.5 code ring face
z 31.0 cover lens top
z 28.5 panel glass top
z 26.0 seat face, display sits here
z 24.0 seat flange under
z 18.9 wheel post underside

r 83.20 bore
r 87.70 knob and rim
NOTES
About 53 LEDs on a 100 per metre strip, 5.0 wide and 1.6 thick, standing
VERTICALLY on the wall's outer face at r 84.0 - 85.6, z 8.25 - 13.25. v15
stood the strip up on the wall; v9 lay a flex ring flat on the plate at r
58.8 and fired outward across the gap.
Diffuser r 85.8 inside, 86.7 - 87.7 outside (bottom to top, flush with the
knob and the rim at r 87.7), so it leans 1.0 over the band's 5.5 height.
Retained by a lip at r 86.7, z 13.5 - 14.3, with a 0.6 shadow gap under
the knob skirt.
Continuous through 360 deg. Standing the strip on the wall takes it clear
of everything inside: the motor at 90 deg reaches r 83.8 with its band,
and the strip's back face is at r 83.9. Nothing now breaks the ring.
Peak draw 2.54 A at full white (12.7 W at 5 V) for 53 LEDs at 48 mA each.
That is what sizes the converter, the halo feed and its connector; the
sustained level is a firmware limit, not a fuse.
AEDR-8300 at 310 deg on a board at z 26.9, looking UP at a 0.15 code ring
on the crown's underside: ring face z 31.53, r 72.5 - 79.5, in a 0.15
recess so the printed crown and the stuck-on ring finish flush. Nominal
2.00 gap, set by the shim - print the family 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.9 / 1 / 1.1 and
fit the one the bench wants.
Reading from below rather than across the bore leaves the bore smooth for
the wheels and sets the gap by a shim on a flat face, not by the knob's
radial runout.
Display: the panel sits on the seat flange's top face at z 26.0, bonded
with 0.50 tape; glass z 26.5 - 28.48, cover lens r 70.0 x 2.5 thick on
top, to z 30.98. There are no columns and no M4 seat tabs - the inverted
structure prints the seat as one flat face.
The ambient-light sensor is not in this wall: it is in the port face,
looking rearward - see D04.
DETAIL P - HALO 7 : 1
strip at r 84.80
The strip stands on the wall's outer face and fires straight out through the
diffuser: r 85.6 to r 86.7 is 1.1 of acrylic in front of the LEDs.
Bench test the diffuser before committing: see docs HALO-BENCH-TEST.
PLAN - HORIZONTAL SECTION AT z 10.8 scale 0.56 : 1
0 deg USB-C
90 deg motor
310 deg encoder
51 deg blower
About 53 LEDs on a 6.8 deg pitch at r 84.80, unbroken all the way round: on the wall's outer face nothing inside can interrupt it.
The rim ring below carries the vents; this cut is above it, in the halo band. The port slot at 0 deg passes under the halo, through the core.
DETAIL Q - ENCODER AND CODE RING 4.5 : 1
Package top to ring face: 2.00 nominal, set by the shim under the
board, not by the knob's radial runout. The ring is a 0.15 recess
in the crown's underside, so the stuck-on ring finishes flush.
PLAN - HORIZONTAL SECTION AT z 25.5, UNDER THE SEAT FACE scale 0.56 : 1
Dashed rectangle: the panel, 136.5 x 132.2, on the seat face above this cut. Dashed circle: the cover lens, r 70.0.
The seat is one flat face at z 26.0. Panel mass 70 g is carried on the bond, so the tape's area and its peel strength are the fixing.
